facts.statement: The genus Wumengosaurus was first described by Jiang and colleagues in 2008.
The type species of the genus is Wumengosaurus delicatomandibularis.
A second species, Wumengosaurus rotundicarpus, was described by Qin and colleagues in 2021.
facts.quote: subdivision: * W. rotundicarpus Qin et al. 2021

facts.statement: Wumengosaurus was an aquatic reptile that lived during the Middle Triassic in Guizhou, southwestern China.
facts.quote: Wumengosaurus is an extinct aquatic reptile from the Middle Triassic (late Anisian stage) Guanling Formation of Guizhou, southwestern China.

facts.statement: This reptile was relatively small, with a total body length ranging from 95.5 to 130.5 centimeters.
facts.quote: It was a relatively small reptile, measuring 95.5 - 130.5 cm in total body length.

facts.statement: Wumengosaurus was originally classified as a basal eosauropterygian and is typically recovered in this position by phylogenetic studies.
facts.quote: It was originally described as a basal eosauropterygian and usually is recovered as such by phylogenetic analyses

facts.statement: One phylogenetic analysis suggested Wumengosaurus is the sister taxon to Ichthyosauromorpha, though this was not formally repositioned in the classification.
facts.quote: although one phylogeny has placed it as the sister taxon to Ichthyosauromorpha while refraining from a formal re-positioning

facts.statement: In 2023, Xu and colleagues reclassified Wumengosaurus as a derived pachypleurosaurid.
facts.quote: In the 2023 description of Luopingosaurus, Xu et al. recovered Wumengosaurus as a derived pachypleurosaurid

facts.statement: Recent analyses place Wumengosaurus as the sister taxon to the clade containing Luopingosaurus and Honghesaurus.
facts.quote: as the sister taxon to the clade formed by Luopingosaurus and Honghesaurus

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Wumengosaurus as Eosauropterygia.
Wumengosaurus is classified within the class Reptilia.
